comment: Dr. Watts is very nice; however, she is EXTREMELY unorganized, and most of the course is just busy work. You have to do an insane amount of work and participate constantly to get a good grade. She's a relatively easy grader, but the amount of time and things you have to do is not worth it.

Dr Watts was a mediocre professor. Her lectures could get boring at times. There was a lot of reading assignments and after most reading assignment you would have to post to a discussion post. Participation matters a lot but oftentimes she is just looking for her answer and not others opinions. Her tests have information not discussed in class.

Professor Watts is extremely unorganized and confusing. She doesn't have a syllabus, but spreads it out through different tabs in blackboard that are hard to find. Her lectures are long and hard to follow. The homework is not hard, but it is a lot and most of the time just feels like busy work.
Super unorganised and unclear instructions

I loved prof Watts for the French Revolution course. She is very accessible outside of class and truly wants her students to succeed. Definitely DONOT take this course if youre looking for an easy A/gen ed, be ready to put the work in. She talks A LOT and is super passionate, so get ready for long, at times painful lectures. Overall wonderful prof.

Dr. Watts was a solid professor regarding lectures and teaching styles. The course had a lot of reading. I felt grading for this course was somewhat arbitrary based on the teacher's viewpoint, where work I submitted felt to be graded too harshly for an introductory history class. I would recommend taking another history professor at UR.

Dr. Watts is a good prof. She is extremely knowledgable about the French Revolution and genuinely has a passion for the subject. There is a good amount of reading and most of the homework is discussion posts. These are once a week, so not too bad. Overall, I enjoyed her class a great deal.

Dr. Watts is great. She's really caring and knows genuinely everything about the French Revolution. She  does give a good amount of homework, but its usually just a discussion board post that's graded on completion. I only wrote 2 essays for the class and we had 1 test. There is a good amount of reading but it's not too bad.
Really cares about students and connections with them. Very accommodating and helpful with assignments. 100% would take again, just a lot of reading but class is mostly discussions.

She's the worst professor I have taken so far here at UR. The workload for her FYS was insane and she'll only talk about the things she's passionate about (French cuisine and revolution) and expect you to be as passionate as her. DO NOT TAKE HER unless you feel passionate about either of those topics or are looking for a challenge.

Dr. Watts is your typical history professor: obsessed with a very unique and small slice of history (French cuisine), and she expects you to feel the same. Homework for this FYS class was ridiculous, especially the constant overlapping papers due. In class, she isn't very demanding, but the workload is a lot. Grading isn't bad, but the work is.

Dr. Watts is very nice, but I can't say I enjoyed my time in her class. I took her for HIST 239, French Revolution. Most classes are devoted to a role-play of the French Revolution or a "Lives and Voices" project where you write historical fiction about the revolution. Good for an easy A, but not very engaging as a history class.

I really enjoyed Dr. Watts as a professor, and I learned a lot from her thought-provoking discussions. This class was a lot of work for a FYS and the readings required analytical thinking. If you aren't up for challenging material or prepared for difficult essay prompts and tough grading, then I do not suggest you take Social Utopias.

She is a cool person overall, but a really tough grader, especially for an FYS. I found it difficult to understand her essay prompts and there was a lot of reading. The class discussions were always interesting and I enjoyed the subjects we learned. She gave great feedback on my writing which was helpful.

Had her for Social Utopias, she's really nice as a person but had really poorly written essay prompts. Workload was manageable but readings were classical era (so if Plato and Rousseau aren't your thing, definitely pass on this one). Directions were vague and there aren't a ton of assignments so each one counts a LOT (even basic reflections).

I know I didn't give Dr. Watts a great score, but she is genuinely a very nice woman. She cares about the health and wellbeing of her students greatly. I felt that she assigned far too much work for an FYS though. Her essay prompts are unclear. Sometimes it feels like she's talking to you as a 5th grader. Hated most of the class. readings are hard

Hard for FYS: social utopias. She honestly is a very good teacher and I feel like I have learned a lot, but she is very hard. Hard grader, not the clearest. Can be intimidating, but honestly shes very cool. Like there were a couple of classes where we just talked for a while which was a breath of fresh air because she can be very difficult.
Dr. Watts is a very caring professor. She is a hard grader but it is easy to excel in her class if you prepare well and actively participate each class.

Dr. Watts is a super sweet lady, and I actually enjoyed having her as my professor. As for the class itself, it was really work heavy (was the course with the most work I had this whole semester). Honestly, I dont think I could take this course again or a course like this again with the amount of work if I have other extremely work heavy courses.

Dr Watts is very accessible outside of class, and she is a very nice person. However, she is also an extremely tough grader, and she assigns an overwhelming amount of readings and assignments. Don't take her class if you care about your grades.
She is a nice person, but her course is just way too many readings, and she's probably the toughest grader I've met. Expect to suffer. There are better courses to take in the history department.

Dr. Watts is a nice lady who cares about her students and subjects she teaches. That being said, her class itself is awful. There are many long readings assigned, tons of homework/papers, and an unreasonable amount of outside work in general each night for a 199 class. Overwhelming and the class itself is discussion based but confusing to follow.
She's the best!
She's there for you when you need her to be. Very supportive. Great help in office hours.

gives lots of reading, relies on participation in class, will give pop quiz if it seems like not enough people are reading/talking in class. pretty approachable in office hours, definitely take advantage of them to show her you want to do well in her class

I would steer clear from her FYS. She grades pretty harshly and sometimes doesnt make clear what she expects from our papers. The reading assignments are heavy but you can probably get away with skimming if youre quick-thinking or you speak well.

Professor Watts is easily my favorite professor at this school. I've gotten an A and a B in the classes I've taken with her and i'm not a genius. She gives you a lot of opportunities to get your grade up. Just meet with her and show that you care and you're good to go. Best advice is to write something that she's interested in and she'll love it.

Dr. Watts is a very nice person. However, she assigns an UNREASONABLE amount of homework. We had to write SO many more essays than the other FYS classes and she is very unclear as to what she expects. The course had a very heavy workload and it was my most time consuming class out of all of my classes which is ridiculous considering it is a FYS.

Dr. Watts is by far the worst professor/teacher I have ever had in my life. Her grading is extremely unfair and she does a terrible job of explaining anything. I can't stress this enough, having her as my professor has been the worst experience of my academic career. Blatantly stated, "a C in my class is like an A in any other class." Terrible.

There is a lot of reading in this class. Small papers due occasionally with a research project and larger paper throughout the semester. Prof. is very knowledgeable and discussions in class helped understanding. Discussions are based on reading so that is very important.

Knows how to design an interesting course. The course objectives are clear and every assignment has a purpose. If you want a professor who knows how to pander to your intellectual curiosity, take whatever she offers. On the other hand, her grading is bizarre. It isn't uncommon for students to share their frustration about a C or D+.

Great professor, definitely challenging, but she's always willing to meet w/ you if you have questions.  Lots of reading, which she will test you on. Class discussions were boring, mainly because she dumbed them down for the ppl who didn't bother doing the reading.  Don't let the 100 level designation fool you-hard class, lots of writing.

Great professor -- v. interesting and helpful.  Certainly tough, yes, but always willing to help students.  Wonderful to talk to for anything! Work hard, go to class, be prepared, and ask for help if needed!

Prior to taking this class I consulted rate my professor and was seriously dreading having to take her upper level history class. The work load was heavy but overall her grading was surprisingly lenient. She was also always willing to meet outside of class. Overall, I'm glad I took the class and didn't listen solely to rate my professor.

Crazy hard paper grader.  If you go to her she'll tell you what you need to do but accomplishing it isn't always easy.  She leads discussions well and class is fairly interesting.  Come to class (duh, it's CORE) and she will respect you a lot more.  Genuinely nice and definitely intelligent.
I didnt learn anything in her class.  I was excited for the course because it sounded interesting and then I got nothing out of it.  Lots of homework but an average grader for history.

ASK FOR HER HELP. i was dying in this class, couldn't keep up with the reading and the pop quizzes. then i went to talk to her, asked for her help with my paper, got probably my only A on a college essay.

I took her witches class and it's pretty much impossible to get a good grade on one of her papers. Take the grade you think you deserve and lower it a letter grade. Tests are too bad if you study. Very nice and helpful though if you go and meet with her.

This should be a 300 level class or should be worth more credit. Gives a rediculous amount of reading. Paper topics are extremely vague and is a VERY hard grader.  Lectures are helpful in terms of interpreting the reading but is closed minded in class discussions.  Material is boring-makes for a long semester unless you're in love with the French.
She's horrendous. If you write a good paper, expect a C.
expect 4+ hours of work a night; should be a 300 level course; she can be snide and close-minded; if you're willing to put in the work you CAN get a good grade
great lecturer, took us out for drinks, super

She expects a lot; however, getting a good grade isn't impossible.  Her tests are extremely straight forward and pretty easy.  She expects too much for the papers though.  A LOT of reading and she expects you to do it all.  Do not take this class unless you are willing to devote a lot of time to it!
If you like tons of work, grades ranging mostly between 90 and 78,  and vague essay topics which will be stringently graded, then this is the class for you.
Very knowledgeable.  Expects a lot ... so be prepared to do a lot of reading.
A very nice woman, but expect a lot of work and reading.  She has high expectations and is very passionate about french history.

An excellent teacher.  Has a reputation for being challenging, but that is often misconstrued by lazy students as being difficult.  A brilliant scholar in her field.  A teacher who EXPECTS that one come to class willing and ready to learn.  Too tough for the immature student!!!
Very good teacher, but a Nazi when it comes to the work load.  If you take her you will learn a lot but expect to devote at least 4+ hours going into each class.  Lots of reading and lots of writing.
She is awful!  She says certain things and then changes her mind and takes off on your papers for it!  I had to transfer out of her class after first semester!  DO NOT TAKE HER!

very unclear.  make sure you brown nose.  also make sure you follow each and every direction perfectly, that'll make her happy.  don't be too intuitive, origionality doesn't have much pull in history class
passionate about the subject and is willing to talk to students for help. Decent class discussions. Fair grader.
